content.text: {"id":"a4fb1787-e388-49a6-b478-933534f004db","audio_id":"a2c1cfcd-13b7-4ff5-8182-1c9d6fdd7bbb","status":"complete","created_at":"2026-11-16T05:01:39Z","answer":"The track retains the bright, cute feminine nursery-pop character: a high, lightly breathy voice sings with a bouncy, tuneful sing-song cadence, not a hard-processed word-drill delivery. Korean diction is generally clear, and both 고양이 and 강아지 are audible as complete words in repeated call-and-response lines. The verse-to-hook transitions sound natural; the short repeated phrases are rhythmic rather than genuinely chopped or unnaturally rushed. The groove is steady and upbeat, with a rounded bouncing bass, clipped rhythm-guitar chords, and crisp clap-like accents. Tempo measures 114.3 BPM in 4/4, close to the stated 113.8 BPM. Vocals start around 0:02 and continue through the ending at about 1:15; the last sung phrase begins around 1:14, but the available lyric alignment only catches “다음에 또 놀…” and misses the final syllable, so I can’t confirm from that text whether the audible line finishes completely. There is no long mid-song instrumental break; the brief gaps between vocal phrases are part of the arrangement. The alignment’s occasional odd or duplicated word labels are transcription/alignment misses, not evidence that the Korean words themselves are chopped."}
